description:
How do you lift a 5,000-tonne ship nearly 10 stories -- while saving water?
At China's Pinglu Canal, the Madao Hub uses three giant water-saving basins to recycle water from the ship lock, cutting water use by more than 60% compared with conventional locks.
The lock also features two 300-meter-long chambers and can handle up to 12 vessels of 5,000 tonnes at the same time.
So, how does it all work? Take a look.
#PingluCanal #China #ShipLock #Engineering #Infrastructure #Innovation #Science
title: Inside China's new ship lock that breaks 3 world records

author: New China TV
description:
A 60-second look at key milestones in the Pinglu Canal's four-year construction.
The 134.2-km waterway, which opened to navigation on Wednesday, runs from Nanning, capital of south China's Guangxi, to the Beibu Gulf, the closest maritime outlet for much of southwest China. It was designed for vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes.  
It is the first river-to-sea canal project planned and coordinated at the national level since the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949.
title: 60 seconds to witness the key millstones of China's new canal
